summary:
Landfill Lens is an environmental monitoring and decision-support platform designed to track changes around landfill sites using Earth observation data. It focuses on vegetation health through the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), land surface temperature, and rainfall as environmental context.
The platform compares conditions around landfill locations with nearby reference areas to help identify localized environmental trends. It applies statistical methods, including the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope, to detect and measure changes over time. It also demonstrates time-series forecasting and rule-based alerts that highlight patterns requiring further investigation.
Landfill Lens addresses the challenge of understanding long-term Earth system changes by making environmental observations easier to explore and interpret. It aims to support environmental authorities, landfill operators, and researchers in monitoring sites and prioritizing further investigation.
details:
Landfill Lens is a web-based environmental monitoring and decision-support prototype designed to identify and analyze environmental changes around landfill sites.

The platform examines selected locations using two spatial areas: a landfill analysis buffer and a surrounding reference area. It focuses on vegetation health using NDVI, land surface temperature, and precipitation as environmental context.

The analysis workflow includes monthly data organization, spatial comparison, statistical trend detection, forecasting, and rule-based alerts. The Mann-Kendall test identifies monotonic trends, while Sen's slope estimates their rate of change. Forecasting methods use historical time-series observations to estimate possible future patterns.

The platform includes an interactive map, environmental trend charts, site comparisons, forecast visualizations, and investigation recommendations. Its intended users include environmental authorities, landfill operators, and researchers who need to monitor environmental changes over time.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It uses Google Earth Engine for the planned satellite-data export workflow, Leaflet for interactive mapping, Chart.js for data visualization, and Tailwind CSS for the interface. The data workflow references Landsat 8, Landsat 9, and NASA GPM IMERG Version 07.

The prototype currently uses simulated demonstration data by default. It includes a Google Earth Engine script designed to export real satellite observations for upload and analysis. Automated live satellite-data integration remains a future development step.

Its main contribution is bringing spatial comparison, statistical trend analysis, forecasting, and investigation alerts into one platform focused on landfill surroundings. The results are intended to identify patterns for further investigation, not to establish environmental damage or prove causation.

AI tools, including ChatGPT and Gemini, assisted with code development, editing, and written content. The team reviewed and adapted the generated material.
